summary: Incomplete stream session after edge proxy TCP RST; client resume yields truncated JSON and duplicated tokens
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a streaming session (SSE and websocket fallback) that ends with a truncated final JSON object after an upstream TCP reset from the corporate edge proxy. When the client attempts to resume the session using the session token the resumed stream contains a partial JSON terminal chunk and sometimes duplicated trailing tokens, causing the SDK to raise a parse error and the app to show incomplete responses.

Impact: Intermittent but reproducible for Acme Analytics (dedicated tenant) on us-east region. Affects long-running generations (>60s) behind certain corporate proxies. Multiple user-facing completions were cut off mid-sentence. Customer production alerts triggered and some requests retried by client resulted in duplicated trailing text.

Environment: prod (dedicated pool), region us-east-1, node pool redwood-ded-3, fronted by customer edge proxy -> our edge-router -> api-gateway.

Observed behavior: final JSON chunk lacks closing "choices" array delimiter and sometimes gets an extra partial token emitted after resume. Client SDK error: "Unexpected end of JSON input" or "Duplicate choice tokens detected".

Expected behavior: resume should produce a consistent continuation or a clear end-of-stream marker; no truncated JSON or duplicated tokens.

Attachments: excerpts of client SDK logs, tcpdump capture from customer side (trimmed), edge-proxy logs snippets, and api-gateway logs timestamps.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a long streaming completion (>60s) from the SDK behind an enterprise HTTP proxy that performs connection reuse and aggressive idle timeouts.
2) After ~45-80s force a TCP RST at the proxy (simulated via iptables --reject or intentional proxy restart).
3) Client automatically attempts resume by calling /v1/resume with session token (same request metadata).
4) Observe resumed stream: terminal JSON chunk is truncated or contains duplicated trailing tokens; SDK raises parse error or returns partial final choice.
5) Repeat with websocket transport and observe similar partial final frame behavior when the proxy performs a half-close followed by rotate/hand-off.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Reproduced with customer sample; symptoms match earlier reported SSE truncation tickets but with different failure mode (edge RST instead of keepalive coalescing).
SRE collected tcpdump and edge-proxy logs; proxy resets observed correlate to corporate proxy health-check rotation and aggressive idle timeout (60s).

Hypothesis 1: Edge proxy issues RST causing upstream to half-flush the last buffered chunk; client resume reconnects to a new serving instance which replays cache prefix but the tail fragment was lost, producing truncated JSON.

Hypothesis 2: The streaming framing at the gateway uses a non-atomic write for the terminal chunk; under RST the last write may be partially flushed and not persisted to the session resume store. Resume logic replays prefix + last partial fragment leading to duplicated tokens.
Reproducer: QA team ran a proxy-rst simulation harness and confirmed truncated final chunk and duplicated trailing tokens on resume with both SSE and websocket transports.
SRE noted that our resume-store accepted partial terminal fragments without a closing sentinel; resume logic did not validate fragment completeness before stitching.
comments: Support (Asha Patel) 2026-03-01: Logged issue with Acme Analytics after receiving multiple user complaints. Collected logs and asked for tcpdump. Assigned to SRE for triage.

SRE (Liam Chen) 2026-03-01: Reproduced locally using proxy-rst harness. Observed partial terminal chunk persisted in resume-store. Creating hypothesis to change resume validation. Linking slack thread #support-streams: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C03STREAMS/p1677654321000

Eng (Marta Ruiz) 2026-03-02: Reviewed code paths in serving-runtime and gateway framing. Found that the gateway performs chunk coalescing and writes terminal chunk in two writes under load; RST can cause last write to be lost. Proposing change to write an explicit terminal sentinel (0x04) and atomic flush path.

Support (Asha Patel) 2026-03-02: Provided customer workaround: enable websocket fallback + client-side guard to treat parse errors as retryable with deduplication token. Customer acknowledged and enabled for critical flows.

Eng (Liam Chen) 2026-03-03: Deployed fix to canary pool in us-east: stronger framing (terminal sentinel), resume-store validation (reject partial fragments), and gateway flush->fsync path for terminal chunk. Monitoring for regressions.
resolution: Fix deployed 2026-03-03 to canary in us-east. Changes: (1) gateway now emits an explicit terminal sentinel ("\u0004") after each final chunk and performs an atomic flush of the final write; (2) resume-store validates that persisted terminal fragments include the sentinel before stitching; partial fragments are treated as missing and cause a safe fallback to re-generation or model-variant fallback. Customer workaround: enabled websocket fallback and client-level retry-with-dedupe. Post-deploy monitoring for 48h showed no further truncated finals for Acme. Follow-ups: add automated proxy-RST test to CI and update runbook for streaming resume anomalies.
